title: Payment History and the Number of Payoff Plan Drafts — Ridgeline Consumer Credit
content:
**Credit risk table — payoff plan drafts.** In a Ridgeline Consumer Credit deferred-interest payoff plan, the deferred-interest balance, as increased for the plan, is divided by the number of plan drafts and rounded up to the next whole dollar. The number of plan drafts rests on the account's own payment history in the last 12 months (dated less than 12 full months before today):

| Payment history on the account in the last 12 months | Number of plan drafts |
|---|---|
| a payment on the account was returned unpaid | the number of the plan's due dates multiplied by 0.5 (halved) and rounded up to a whole number |
| no payment returned unpaid, but a late fee was charged on the account | the number of the plan's due dates multiplied by 0.75 and rounded down to a whole number |
| no payment returned unpaid and no late fee charged | the full number of the plan's due dates |

In every case the number of plan drafts is never fewer than 1.

## Worked counts (hypothetical numbers of due dates)

| Plan's due dates | Returned payment in 12 months | Late fee only | Neither |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 5 | 7 (7.5 rounded down) | 10 |
| 7 | 4 (3.5 rounded up) | 5 (5.25 rounded down) | 7 |
| 1 | 1 (0.5 rounded up) | 1 (0.75 rounded down is 0, raised to 1) | 1 |

## Points of judgement

- A returned payment in the 12 months decides the row whether or not a late fee was also charged.
- A returned payment or a late fee dated exactly 12 full months before today falls outside the window.

**Hypothetical:** a plan-increased balance of 1995.00 over 10 due dates, with one late fee in the last 12 months and no returned payment, is divided by 7: 285.00.
